The project also comes with a playground to play and edit MML in real time, and a converter that can convert from tracker formats and NES/SNES/GameBoy/Genesis music straight to MML. It's all open source under MIT, and the link has a bunch of example songs to listen to. Happy to answer any questions.

Show HN: I built an infinite canvas to explore 340k artworks from The Met
show_hn.story_text:
Hey HN! I built this project, Open Metropolitan, which is a digital museum that uses The Met's Open Access data to give people the ability to explore hundreds of thousands of artworks in The Met's collection, since they would need a space as big as Central Park to display it all. I love the experience of wandering through a museum and stopping to look at whatever catches my eye. I wanted to recreate that feeling digitally, rather than using a traditional, boring website. Open Metropolitan lets you: - Explore over 340k artworks on an infinite canvas.
- Select any artwork and discover visually similar pieces.
- Search the collection using natural language.
- Sort art across centuries using a Time Machine feature. The project is completely free, and I personally pay all the hosting

Show HN: KIZZ – A Build tool that tracks dependencies so you dont have to
show_hn.story_text:
I used to use Fabricate a long time ago, its strace based build was a great idea and I always wanted something that could track dependencies so I didn't have to. KIZZ is that, it tracks your dependencies, and also the order of the build.  It won't rebuild if nothing changes, and can be scripted with literal markdown files with starlark build steps.  I call this building in positive space, not negative space. Linux only because Win/Mac make doing this very very hard on those platforms.
It can also be used to work out dependencies for another build tool, so you're not guessing anymore.
